output.summary: An open-clumping bamboo native to Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia and southern China, it commonly has lemon-yellow stems striped with green. Flowering is uncommon and fruit is rare. Its young shoots are eaten cooked or pickled across Asia; they contain a highly toxic compound that readily breaks down in boiling water.
output.edibilityNote: Young shoots are eaten cooked or pickled across Asia; their highly toxic taxiphyllin readily degrades in boiling water.
